judgement: land-ground slots
not specified: kept the v7.4 land cast without its raptor, bird and sentient slots (apex 1, meso 2, grazer 2, ground prey 2, vermin 3).
ranges
"1-2" and "2-3": each cast draws its count inside the range, so cast sizes vary from season to season.
apex rule

kept as built (the mix): the largest flagged predator in season keeps the apex slot; the others can take meso. With full pools this makes the apex the same species in every season it is in season (see the diversity table).
river-only apex
no apex slot (your list has none); flagged predators there can take the meso slot.
fill fallback

a slot with room and no candidate linked to the cast is filled anyway from its eligible species ("no link"), so no slot stays empty while candidates exist; the food web is computed after the draw on every layer, as you asked for land-flying.
amphibians

an amphibious (water-breathing, not aquatic) creature never enters land-ground; if its BIOME names a fort land biome it can enter the freshwater layer (its shore slot), and on a saltwater marsh, swamp or mangrove the ocean layer.
shore and fliers
a shore creature or a waterbird eats an aquatic creature no larger than itself (or 20,000 cm3), and aquatic vermin.
murky pools

"small" = adult size up to 20,000 cm3 for the pool mini roster; DF's pool fish and amphibians are vermin (lungfish, pond turtle, toad), so the pool's fish slot draws fish-class and amphibious vermin too (a species drawn as fish is not also drawn as vermin).
cavern sentients
a sentient cavern species (troll, blind cave ogre, gorlak, animal people, troglodyte) fills only the sentient slot.
weirdness

a first-cut 0-1 score per cavern species (table in the step-through); cavern 1 picks weight (1-w)^2, cavern 2 the middle, cavern 3 w^2. DF's own raw depth range still decides which caverns a species can live in.
region biomes
a real fort's biomes are the 3x3 world tiles around it (DF draws a block's wildlife from all nine region neighbours); each biome takes the savagery and evil of the nearest tile that has it.
alignment
GOOD species only where the biome is good (evil 0-32), EVIL only where evil (66+); cavern species are exempt (v7: alignment only limits taming).
cavern savagery
caverns ignore surface savagery: DF stocks savage cave species (giant cave spider) on calm forts.
extinct rule

DF's raws tag every real-world-extinct species SAVAGE; the world's REAL_WORLD_EXTINCT setting is read in place of that tag (UNTAMED_WILDS and ISOLATED: savage regions only; WILDERNESS and DOMESTICATED: any wild region). Extinct animal people stay savage-only, as all animal people.
extinct setting
region19's REAL_WORLD_EXTINCT cannot be read without DF (world.raws.param_real_world_extinct); the real forts assume UNTAMED_WILDS, the install's default preset value.
wild
a creature is wild when it has a BIOME and either LARGE_ROAMING or a vermin tag, colony insects (VERMIN_SOIL_COLONY: ants, bees, termites) included (DF's own test for region populations).

extinct_rule.ISOLATED: only in isolated savage regions (small savage islands and patches)
extinct_rule.DOMESTICATED: in any wild region (and kept by civilisations)
